# Which Python versions still get security fixes in October 2026?

Python 3.10 reached end of life on 1 October 2026. See which versions get security fixes, what each status means, and how to plan an upgrade.

SS

Safeguard Security Team

3 min read

As of 19 October 2026, Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 receive security fixes only, and 3.14 and 3.15 receive bug and security fixes. Python 3.10 reached end of life on 1 October 2026, so it gets no further changes, and 3.9 ended on 31 October 2025.

This comes from the Python Developer's Guide status of versions page, fetched on the review date below. Dates in italics there are scheduled and can change.

| Version | Status | First release | End of life |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 3.14 | bugfix | 2025-10-07 | 2030-10 (scheduled)

A complete guide to Python version lifecycles, support phases, and critical end-of-life dates from 3.8 through 3.14

Python powers everything from machine learning pipelines to enterprise web applications, but every Python version has an expiration date.

When a version reaches end of life (EOL), the Python Software Foundation stops releasing security patches, leaving your applications exposed to newly discovered vulnerabilities.

With Python 3.10 reaching end of life on **October 31, 2026**, just weeks from now, and Python 3.15 entering release candidate stage, the landscape is shifting fast.
